metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my cousin's clothing boutique called Thread & Loom in Pune. it sells handloom kurtas, sarees, cotton shirts and dupattas. people should be able to browse products by category, filter by size and price, see a size guide, check new arrivals, and order on whatsapp. also show a lookbook section with styled outfits, the store timings and location, the return and exchange policy, and a few customer reviews. it should feel earthy and elegant and work well on phones

estimate_vs_charged.name: Product catalogue with filters and WhatsApp ordering

review.verdict: A clean, low-cost run that reached a workable site in 2 cycles with 0 redirects and 0 conflicts, but the filter and WhatsApp behaviour was never executed, and the negotiation and HOLD paths were never exercised.

identity.note: Got every fact in one round [2][4] and closed accurately [54]. Pushed a cosmetic tap-size finding to the Requester [37] instead of ruling on it, and [40] drifts into how to fix it.

adaptation.note: Reused a playbook and kept a 25 reserve [7]. Split the fixes cleanly by section ownership [41] and saved a lesson [53][55]. Spent 8 of the reserve on a low-severity head warning.

priority.note: Arithmetic checked (15+50+6x10=125) and the reserve protected [8][42]. Granted everything and never countered, so its bargaining role is untested.

coordination.note: Followed its stated rule and gave a contingency order [13]. Messages run 5-6 sentences and repeat the rule each time, against the 1-3 sentence rule. It also tells Audit what to check.

audit.note: Named the failed criterion (R-6) and the extra title warning [36], and was honest in [52] that filters were read in code, not clicked. Marked all 16 done-when items as passing on code reading alone.

W-1.note: Scaffold was sound and said it was unrun [12]. Its section left a duplicate title that W-10 later removed [49].

W-2.note: Largest piece: 10 products, filters, wa.me order links, no Audit findings [15][52]. Behaviour checked by code reading only.

W-3.note: Exactly the 3 arrivals, no Audit findings [18].

W-4.note: Exactly 3 outfits from listed products, empty photo spots [21].

W-5.note: Chest sizes as supplied, nothing invented [24].

W-6.note: Content correct [27], but the phone and Instagram links were 22px tall at 360px [35].

W-7.note: Ordering, delivery and exchange terms match the brief [30].

W-9.note: Fixed the tap targets within its envelope [46]; the re-measure shows 0 small targets [51].

W-10.note: Removed the duplicate title and escaped the ampersand without touching anything else [49].

went_well: 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 validator refusals, 0 failed workflows across 43 turns; all 10 workflows done.
Charter had 16 checkable done-when items and nothing left to be confirmed. Content matches the brief (10 products, 3 outfits, 3 reviews).
Budget held: 141 of 150, with fixes paid from the reserve set aside up front [8][42].
Builders said plainly they had only read code, never run it [12][15][18]. The code check caught the tap-size problem [35] and confirmed the fix [51].
problems: Done-when items on category browse, size and price filters, and the prefilled WhatsApp message were only read in code [15][52], yet the run is marked Done.
Cycle 1 failed on a 44px tap target rule that is not in the charter standards [7]. The department could not know it, and it cost a cycle, 16 budget and a human pause.
The Requester was asked about a cosmetic finding [37] with 125 of 150 spent. The system text there says items are 'to be confirmed' while to_be_confirmed is empty, so the limit trigger is unclear.
Priority and Coordination took 22 of 43 turns with 0 counters, refusals or holds. Charged cost equals the estimate for every workflow (rate card), so the envelope check never tested anything.
Identity, Adaptation and Audit each had only 2 to 5 turns, so conclusions about them are thin.
learnings: Add a headless-browser check that clicks the category buttons, applies size and price filters, and reads the order link's wa.me href and message. The renderer already runs at 360 and 1280 [35][51].
Decide whether design rubrics like R-6 should be visible to Adaptation up front. Next test: rerun this brief with the saved playbook [55] and see if cycle 1 passes. One run is thin evidence.
Check what actually triggered the limit pause at [37] and fix its wording. Consider letting Identity rule on low-severity findings and ask the Requester only when budget or cycles truly run out.
Test negotiation with a tighter budget (for example 100 against the 125 plan) to force a COUNTER or HOLD. This run gives no evidence on those paths.
Try fewer, larger workflows. One write lock serialises everything [10], so 8 workflows bought no parallelism. Untested whether it is cheaper or has fewer defects.
Keep the reserve and the one-writer section ownership; both worked [42][43].

events.detail: Only you can close what's left: these done-when items are to be confirmed.
